title: Go on a trip to the beyond with these paranormal destinations
excerpt: If you're looking for a holiday experience that will get the blood pumping, why not try one of our perfectly curated paranormal destinations?
content:
It's no surprise that horror films and television shows have been increasing in popularity of late. But if you're looking to take your fascination with all things spooky and paranormal to the next level, take a trip to the beyond with these destinations and experiences.

According to a report from Booking.com, 62% of Australians have an appetite for using their precious holiday time to encounter paranormal activities. With more than half of the population curious about the afterlife, death and spirituality, it makes sense that some are taking that curiosity a step further. It also explains why staying at paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren's house has become a fully booked experience.

And while personally, this is an experience I'd rather enjoy virtually, through a fictional scenario on television, this is for the ones that would like to lift that veil. So, without further ado, if you're looking for a little adventure or a holiday experience that will get the blood pumping, why not try one of our curated paranormal destinations below?

Warren House

Ed and Lorraine Warren found themselves in the spotlight in the last decade through the hit anthology The Conjuring. A personal favourite of mine. If you've seen the films, you'll know they're based off true stories, and that all those objects that were possessed have been collected and stored safely in the Warrens house. If you ever find yourself in Monroe, Connecticut you can visit the house, and even stay a night. Paranormal sightings are frequent with guests reporting seeing shadows of figures, light flickering, feelings of oppressive energy and disembodied noises.

The Stanley Hotel

The Shining is one of my favourite movies, so I can wholeheartedly say this might be the only experience I would stay at. The Stanley Hotel is located at Estes Park, Colorado, the very hotel that inspired Stephen King to write his novel The Shining, which was later adapted for film by Stanley Kubrick. Built in 1909 it's one of America's most haunted sites. If you're staying around the area for the ski season, here are some tips to know to make the most out of a paranormal visit. Room 217 is one of the active rooms in the hotel – it's where Stephen King stayed, and is associated with the spirit Elizabeth Wilson, a chambermaid who survived a 1911 gas explosion, who is said to tidy belongings in the room when you stay. Apparently Jim Carrey stayed in that room when they filmed Dumb and Dumber, and checked out within a few hours. The fourth floor is also one of the most active hearing noises, while the main staircase is believed to be an energetic hub for lingering spirits.

Quarantine Station

One of Australia's most haunted sites is Manly's Quarantine Station. Opened in 1832, it closed two years later in 1984 and has since been Australia's longest operating quarantine station. It was a station where people were detained to prevent infectious diseases like smallpox, bubonic plague and Spanish flu from spreading to Sydney's population. Since its closure it has been reserved as part of Sydney Harbour National Park where tours and conferences can be held. But due to the nature of the site, and with over 500 recorded passings at the station, encounters have since been a frequent thing. The hospital wards and gravediggers cottage are the most active sites with reports of noises, chairs being moved and voices being heard. And luckily for you, you can also stay the night at this station, or if that isn't for you, a night tour is also available.

Port Arthur Historic Site

I have actually visited this site in Tasmania. A UNESCO World Heritage Site that was built around 1870's as a timber station for Australia, it laterevolved into a harsh secondary punishment prison for reoffending male convicts . It is a massive site that takes a full day to explore. Due to its history and age there have been quite a few paranormal sightings. With ghost tours hosted regularly at night, guests have been said to hear sounds of children laughing, sounds of bodies being disembodied, and even see sightings of reoccurring spirits that lived on the site decades ago.

Dalhousie Castle

One of Scotland's oldest castles' located in Bonnyrigg is also one of the country's most haunted locations. The most common spirit to be seen in the castle is ] Lady Catherine from the 16th-Century, a mistress to one of the Ramsay Laird's who was punished by his jealous wife. She can be seen roaming the staircases, corridors and turrets. And legend has it, she isn't a fan of bagpipes, so if you stay the night, perhaps keep the tunes off. And if staying the night isn't your thing, there are ghost tours for the castle and opportunities to dine in the dungeon where sightings are quite common.

Old Changi Hospital 

I lived in Singapore for 12-years, and this was a location I got to know to avoid. With the country's young history, this was built only in 1930's as a British Royal Airforce hospital, during the fall of Singapore in 1942 when the Japanese overtook the country it became a prisoner-of-war camp. After World War two, it reopened as a hospital. In 1997 it closed down, after merging with Tao Payoh Hospital to form the Changi General Hospital. And since its closure due to its dark history, people who visit the area have come across some dark sightings. While you aren't allowed inside the building, there is no need, the activity is strong all around.
